evidence: English Journey, The Edwardians, Journey Down a Rainbow and the other literary works give J. B. Priestley about 21/30 listed thesis-work citations. Herodotus and Hellenistic Culture and the Alcman article are Jessica Priestley's; the Birmingham religious works and autobiography are Joseph Priestley's; respiratory resistance credits J. G. Priestley.

A History of the Modern Middle East, Islam against the West and The Making of an Arab Nationalist are William L. Cleveland's. The Elements of Graphing Data, Visualizing Data and the three regression/smoothing records belong to statistician William S. Cleveland: approximately 32/37 listed thesis-work citations belong to the key.

Nearly all listed citations (43/45) are Kai-wing Chow's, led by Printing and Book Culture in Late Imperial China, Publishing, Culture, and Power, and The Rise of Confucian Ritualism. The two-citation exception, Introduction: On Chineseness as a Theoretical Problem, is explicitly credited to Rey Chow by the publisher.

Comercio clandestino de esclavos, Las conspiraciones de 1810 y 1812, La gesta heroica del Triunvirato and the other Cuban/Caribbean histories give José Luciano Franco 14/33 listed citations. Proteção à Natureza e Identidade Nacional and the environmental works with Drummond belong to José Luiz de Andrade Franco. The two-citation 'et al' record is unresolved.

When Nationalism Began to Hate (21 citations), Faith and Fatherland, Christianity and Modernity in Eastern Europe and the Polish-history essays are Brian Porter-Szűcs's, as his CV confirms. Brian Ernest Porter accounts for The Aberystwyth Papers, the Martin Wight article and Britain and the Rise of Communist China: about 4/40 listed citations.

Conservatism in America Since 1930, Cadres for Conservatism and The Conservative Century are Gregory L. Schneider's; with the Reagan chapter, about 23/36 listed citations. The Way of the Cross Leads Home, The Ritual of Happy Dying and Social Religion are A. Gregory Schneider's (13 citations). The key's share is approximately, but slightly below, two thirds.

John Mark Carroll's Hong Kong and Canton works account for 21/31 listed citations. The Black Military Experience and Buffalo Soldiers West are John Melvin Carroll's; Fritz Pollard and Red Grange are John Martin Carroll's. Couching Counterfactuals credits James Edward Carroll, and An Evolutionary Paradigm credits Joseph Carroll. The fragment 'and ed' remains unresolved.

Full Circle, Facing the Dictators, The Reckoning, Another World and the speeches and foreign-policy records are Anthony Eden's; his memoirs dominate. Social Life in a Provincial University is Alice Eden's article, the one clear namesake exception. Estimated key share: 32/33 listed thesis-work citations, nearly all.

The leading Munitions and Supply history (9 citations) is J. de N. Kennedy's; The Business of War (3) is Sir John Noble Kennedy's; Bahian Elites (4 across two records) explicitly credits John Norman Kennedy. The presidential addresses belong to John F. Kennedy. No listed work is securely attributable to John Pendleton Kennedy.

Wild West Shows (18 citations), Indian Lives (4), The Indian Man (2) and the other Native American-history records give Lester George Moses about 28/31 listed citations. Epic Themes in the Secret History of the Mongols and Introduction to Mongolian History and Culture are Larry W. Moses's; A Survey of Urban Economics is Leon N. Moses's.
